evidence.notes:
Design: the projection builds a placeholder object that shares one string per allowance and references the packet's own strings, then measures it with jsonLongerThan. Neither queue nor start builds a JSON copy. The sort order is replaced by a string two characters shorter than its allowance, so it takes the same JSON length as a 25-character number. Production code imports nothing from src/test/. The ticket guessed 24 for the longest number; testing found 25 (-0.0000012345678901234567), so the allowance is 25.

Red-team review:
- Bypass paths: only queueTransfer writes transfer rows (grep of INSERT INTO transfers), and startTransfer covers packets stored by older builds. An agent session already in progress under an older build could keep calling record_transfer_item without calling start_transfer again. It is not refused there. This is out of the ticket's scope, and the read-back check still stops completion.
- Fail-open: a malformed stored packet_json makes the projection throw a TypeError. Before this change nextRefs threw on the same input, so nothing regressed and the start is not allowed. The refusal sits after requireOpenTransfer and before every write, and runs inside withIdempotency's transaction.
- Seams: the read-back check, assertWithinReadbackLimits, is unchanged and stays the backstop. Two kinds of faithful read-back are not covered, as the ticket's 'DM text exactly' rule implies. Linear may rewrite text longer, for example by adding Markdown escapes the comparison tolerates. Linear may also report extra relation kinds that the comparison ignores. Both are documented in the runbook as cases where the submit-time check still refuses. skills/linear-transfer.md and src/mcp/transferKickoff.ts do not mention the new start refusal; its message tells the agent to ask the person to cancel.
- Vacuous tests: the boundary test pins equality (refused at size-1, accepted at size), and the undercount mutation shows the 'never below' tests catch undercounting. Restoring the base files shows every new test fails.
- Realistic plans: a typical 1,000-ticket plan projects to under 0.5% of the limit, and one with 2,600-character bodies to about 3.1%, so none is refused.

outputs.summary: Added projectedReadbackLongerThan(packet, max) in src/core/transfer/linearReadback.ts. It builds the merged read-back a packet implies (project, milestones, issues and relations). Every DM text and label is kept exactly as the packet gives it, priorities are exact, and relation kinds are 'blocks' or 'related' from the packet. Each Linear-supplied value is a placeholder sized by its READBACK_ALLOWANCES allowance. The result is measured with jsonLongerThan, so keys, quotes and escapes count as they do for a submitted read-back. READBACK_ALLOWANCES sits next to READBACK_LIMITS in src/core/schemas.ts, with a comment saying the values are allowances, not limits: id 64, identifier 32, url LIMITS.shortText (2,000, the most linearUrl accepts), milestoneId 64, stateType 16, sortOrder 25 (the longest JSON of any number, e.g. -0.0000012345678901234567), relationEnd 64. queueablePacket in src/core/services/transfers.ts now refuses a packet over READBACK_LIMITS.totalChars. It runs after the existing refusals and before any row is written, and fails with invalid_input, { limit: 'totalChars', max } and a message saying the plan is too large to transfer. startTransfer parses the stored packet and makes the same check before any UPDATE or event, with a message telling the agent to ask the person to cancel the transfer. The runbook's Size limits section (docs/runbooks/linear-transfer.md) documents the queue-time check, the allowance table and the start refusal, and the 'Authorize it in the app' refusal list now includes it. Measured projections: the typical 1,000-ticket test plan projects to 475,362 characters; 1,000 tickets with 2,600-character bodies to 3,079,362; 1,000 tickets with full LIMITS.markdown bodies to 100,479,362, which is refused.

evidence.notes: Risk trace: buildRunHistoryRecord (portable.ts:758) reads only rows keyed by run_id: runs, attempts, sprint_reports, checkpoints, row_checks. applyEpic (importer.ts:772) writes only epics, plan_revisions, ticket_status, sync_state(kind='epic') and search_index; none of those is read by the run export. Runs/attempts/reports/checkpoints/row_checks are written by applyRun only, and planRuns still skips any run with a pending/failed outbox row matching run_id (hasPendingRunChanges). Every production run_history enqueue (runs.ts:65, attempts.ts:122, checkpoints.ts:687/775, execution.ts:278/468, reports.ts:295, rowChecks.ts:85, adoption.ts:228) sets runId, so each is guarded that way. pauseActiveRuns does update runs, but it runs only on a branch change and does not depend on the predicate. Conclusion: importing the epic cannot change the pending run export. The c3 test pins this byte for byte: the run.json flushed after the import equals the record built before the reconcile. Callers: (1) importer.ts planEpics: the epic now imports when its only waiting exports are run_history/comment; planRuns then no longer drops all of the epic's runs, but runs with their own pending exports still get the 'Tracked history for run' conflict (intended). (2) storage.ts choiceStands (src/core/repo/storage.ts:55, not services/): a stored 'Tracked records for epic' conflict whose epic has only run_history waiting is now resolvable:false. It is stale, and the next reconcile imports the epic and clears it via markSynced. (3) epicConflict.ts requireConflict: with only run_history waiting it now refuses with 'nothing to choose' for both keep=tracked and keep=local (before, it allowed the choice). (4) epicConflict.ts keepTracked (left unchanged, as instructed): its post-flush hasPendingEpicChanges check (line 79, 'its run history is still waiting to be exported') can no longer fire for run_history, so if the scoped run_history flush fails, keepTracked now continues to reconcile. That is safe: the run with the failed export gets a run conflict instead of an overwrite. The pre-flush and the error branch are now effectively dead; this is for DM-367. Red-team: (a) the first storage test was vacuous: insertRevision defaults to state 'pending', and a pending plan revision alone made the choice resolvable. I fixed it with state:'saved' and re-showed the failure without the change. (b) The c3 flush test fails without the change only through its import precondition (result.imported); the flushed bytes are the same either way. That is by design: it shows that the import does not change the export. (c) Bypass check: a run_history row without run_id would escape hasPendingRunChanges, but no production code enqueues one, and the finalizer's run_history handler requires run_id. (d) Pre-existing, not changed here: the flush after the import overwrites the other machine's changed run.json with this machine's record (the run conflict stays recorded). See discoveries. (e) importer.test.ts conflicts describe exceeded max-lines-per-function; I moved the new tests to their own describe block.

evidence.notes:
Red-team. Attacked: (1) Bypass by other writers: the finalizer's profile handler is the only writer of profiles/<name>.json (grep of profileFile/profilesDir). (2) Fail-open: unimportedProfile throws on an unsafe path or a read error (a directory or an unreadable file), so the export fails closed. Storage status catches it and offers no choice. db mode never offers or accepts a choice. (3) Deadlock: Keep tracked marks the export done before reconciling, so scanProfiles no longer skips the profile. Write local sets imported_hash so the guard passes. Both are refused when nothing is in conflict, so neither leaves a stuck state. Remaining wait, the same as runs: a tracked profile the reconcile rejects (bad JSON, over 256 KiB, wrong name) blocks the export and offers no button. The export error says to fix it in Git first. (4) Crash windows: a crash after writing the file and before recordExport commits leaves this machine's own text, which the 'exactly the text to write' rule lets the next flush overwrite. A crash after Write local commits and before its flush leaves imported_hash set, so the next flush writes over only that hash. A newer pull in between is refused again and becomes a fresh conflict. (5) Seams: matchesSync is now shared by the import (profileImport) and the guard, so both use the same hash and the same sync rule. ReconcileResultView.profileConflicts is unchanged. StorageStatusView.profileConflicts gains resolvable, and every producer and fixture is updated. StorageConflictView is narrowed to 'epic'|'run'|'comment', so a profile never enters conflicts[]. (6) Vacuous tests: each new test was shown to fail with its change reverted. The missing-file/row tests do not depend on the guard, so they were shown to fail by switching off the exemption instead. Changed on purpose: the old test 'lets the pending local save win on export' asserted the overwrite this ticket forbids, and it now asserts the refusal. The stored conflict text 'Flush or resolve the local changes before importing' was misleading once flushing is refused, so it now names the Storage card choice. Known behaviour kept from the spec: before any sync_state row exists (no reconcile yet), a flush still writes over a pulled profile ('missing row writes as today'). After a reconcile, storeProfileConflicts creates a row (with null hashes), so the guard then protects the file and the choice is offered.

Discoveries:
- title: Offer a way out when a tracked record the reconcile rejects blocks its own export
  reason: For profiles (as for runs after DM-367), a tracked file that is unimported and also rejected by the reconcile (bad JSON, oversized, names another profile) keeps the waiting export refused. No conflict row and no Storage card choice exist for it; the only guidance is the export error text 'must be fixed in Git first'. Seen while red-teaming src/core/repo/finalizer.ts exportProfile and src/core/repo/storage.ts profileConflictsOf.

outputs.summary: Profile exports no longer write over a tracked profiles/<name>.json that another machine changed. finalizer.ts exportProfile refuses with conflict when unimportedProfile finds a file whose trackedProfileHash (the hash the export records) is neither exported_hash nor imported_hash of the profile's sync_state row. A missing file, a missing row, or a file already holding exactly the text to write still writes. The file is hashed whatever its size, and an empty file hashes as empty. A refused profile entry blocks only that profile's later entries (its only key is profile:<name>). resolveRecordConflict accepts kind 'profile' (id = profile name). The command schema is now a discriminated union, so a profile id is validated with profileName, not stableId. RESOLVERS maps profile to settleProfileConflict (new services/profileConflict.ts). Keep tracked, in one tx with no file write, marks the waiting profile exports done, reconciles, and requires 'profile:<name>' in imported, else rolls back. Write local sets imported_hash to the found hash, then flushes only that profile (new FlushScope {profileName}). Both are refused unless the tracked file is unimported and a profile export waits; the capability is the same desktop-only repo.resolve_conflict. Storage status profileConflicts now carry resolvable under the same rule, and the StorageCard offers Keep tracked records / Write local sending kind 'profile'. Shell toasts have profile wording. matchesSync is widened to 'profile', and hasPendingProfileChanges moved to syncState.ts (profileImport now uses both). The stored conflict message now names the choice instead of 'Flush or resolve'. docs/architecture.md states the profile rule.
